lease_busy.description: An immediate try for an instance met a holder, or an eligible waiting entry that nobody may jump (Workflow #369). A Lab operation's refusal names who is in the way, before any frame or input: holder_kind is the holder's kind on a held instance, or the waiting entry's kind on a free one, where queue_position is that entry's position. A client AcquireLease and the Runtime's dedicated leases are refused with this code too. Registered once in the contract (A2a D3); the host and the scheduler emit it.
lease_busy.common_causes: Another client, a scheduled run, a stuck-recovery ladder or an operator request holds the instance or waits for it.
lease_busy.handling: Nothing ran. Retry once the instance is free; actingctl status shows lease_active and queued_request_count.

lease_expired.description: A lease was used, renewed or released after its expiry. Since 0.11.5 it also ends a Runtime-held key (a stuck-recovery ladder, a startup package claim) whose renewal came after the key lapsed: the ladder records its rung failed with this reason and finishes. Registered once in the contract (A2a D3); the host and the scheduler emit it.
lease_expired.common_causes: A holder that overran its own step bound; a host that was stopping while a ladder held an instance.
lease_expired.handling: Nothing to repair for a Runtime hold: the next trigger starts a new ladder. A client acquires a new lease.

lease_missing.description: The lease named is no longer the instance's lease. Since 0.11.5 it also ends a Runtime-held key (a stuck-recovery ladder, a startup package claim) whose renewal found the key gone: the ladder records its rung failed with this reason and finishes. Registered once in the contract (A2a D3); the host and the scheduler emit it.
lease_missing.common_causes: Shutdown cancelled the hold, or the key was handed on after it lapsed.
lease_missing.handling: Nothing to repair for a Runtime hold: the next trigger starts a new ladder. A client acquires a new lease.

lease_queue_expired.description: An operator request waited its cap in its instance's one queue without a grant, and its entry was removed (Workflow #369). The waiting requests are a direct task run (CLI, console, MCP ac_run_pack; cap min(60 s, the run's remaining deadline minus a 30 s run budget)), a safe reset or an application lifecycle command (3 s), and a self-check or the reconnect of an instance resume (3 s; a resume is refused before its gate is lifted). timeout_ms is the cap; holder_kind names the instance's holder when it has one; queue_position is the entry's position when it was removed. Its ledger record is the instance-linked scheduler.denied lease_queue_expired at warning. A client QueueLease whose wait ended is refused with this code too. Registered once in the contract (A2a D3); the host and the scheduler emit it.
lease_queue_expired.common_causes: Another client, a scheduled run, a stuck-recovery ladder or another operator request held the instance for longer than the cap; a takeover cooldown after an unclean restart; business capacity refused the grant for the whole cap.
lease_queue_expired.handling: Nothing ran. Retry once the holder named by holder_kind has released the instance; actingctl status shows lease_active and queued_request_count meanwhile.
